title: Trump: U.S. makes deal to deport Americans to El Salvador terrorist prison
description_short: Trump: U.S. makes deal to deport Americans to El Salvador terrorist prison
description_medium: During Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s February 2025 visit, Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele publicly offered to house people deported from the United States in Salvadoran prisons. Reuters described the offer as covering “dangerous criminals”; later reporting said Rubio discussed people of any nationality, potentially including U.S. citizens already serving sentences. The supplied reports do not establish a signed transfer agreement or CECOT as the destination for Americans.
description_long: During Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s February 2025 visit, Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele offered to house people deported from the United States in Salvadoran prisons. Reuters described the offer as covering “dangerous criminals” from anywhere in the world. The supplied draft says later AP reporting described Rubio as saying the offer could include people of any nationality and potentially violent U.S. citizens already serving sentences. Those statements document a public offer and its reported breadth, but the available material does not include a signed agreement authorizing transfers, identify CECOT as the agreed destination for U.S. citizens, or explain the legal authority for moving people from U.S. custody into Salvadoran prisons. It also does not establish that any American was transferred under such an arrangement. The headline’s claim of a deal to send U.S. citizens to a particular prison therefore exceeds the evidence in the supplied reports. The agreement text, destination and transfer records are needed to establish what the governments authorized.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: U.S. makes deal to deport Americans to El Salvador terrorist prison
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: U.S. makes deal to deport Americans to El Salvador terrorist prison

notes: Needs context: the supplied Reuters/AP summaries establish a public offer but not a signed agreement, an agreed CECOT destination for Americans, legal transfer authority, or any transfer. The headline overstates the documented arrangement.
proposed_correction: Describe Bukele’s public offer to house deportees in Salvadoran prisons; reserve any claim about U.S. citizens or CECOT for evidence of the written agreement and transfers.

title: Trump: Social Security Administration calls out DOGE lies
description_short: Trump: Social Security Administration calls out DOGE lies
description_medium: On March 16, 2025, the Social Security Administration responded to Elon Musk’s claim that DOGE had found millions of dead people receiving benefits. The agency said more than three million deaths are reported to it each year and that benefits are stopped when a death is reported. It also distinguished payment errors from fraud, saying most identified overpayments were later recovered.
description_long: The Social Security Administration issued a press release after Elon Musk said DOGE had found “millions of dead people” receiving Social Security payments. The agency explained that more than three million deaths are reported to Social Security each year, but said benefits are terminated when a death is reported. It also addressed concerns that living recipients could be mistakenly listed as deceased. The linked account notes that an audit found some fraud in payments from 2015 through 2022, while describing the overall level as negligible relative to the program’s size. It says many cases labeled as fraud were mistakes that produced overpayments, most of which were later identified and recovered. The agency’s statement disputed the inference that a high number of death reports meant millions of deceased people were collecting benefits. The source also records broader claims by Trump and Musk about waste at Social Security, but the press release alone does not resolve every question about the program’s finances or payment controls.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Social Security Administration calls out DOGE lies
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Social Security Administration calls out DOGE lies

notes: Complete from the supplied synopsis and linked account. The article’s account of SSA’s response is distinguished from broader claims about program solvency and the complete audit record.

title: Trump: DHS: We tricked schools into un-enrolling hundreds of thousands of visa students
description_short: Trump: DHS: We tricked schools into un-enrolling hundreds of thousands of visa students
description_medium: A Department of Homeland Security court filing said that ending a student’s record in the SEVIS database does not itself end the student’s non-immigrant status. The linked account reports that hundreds of student records were terminated and that some universities then removed students from enrollment. It does not establish the headline’s claim that hundreds of thousands of students were affected or that DHS described its actions as a trick.
description_long: A Department of Homeland Security filing addressed the effect of terminating international students’ records in SEVIS, the database used to track students in the United States on visas. The filing quoted in the linked account said a database termination did not itself terminate a student’s non-immigrant status; an agency official also said existing law did not give DHS authority to end that status through the database action alone. The account reports that hundreds of records were terminated and that some universities, believing the students had lost status, removed them from enrollment or advised them to leave. It does not identify the court case, provide a verified total, or explain the grounds for each record termination. The supplied filing language also does not support the headline’s characterization that DHS “tricked” schools, and the source says hundreds of records rather than hundreds of thousands.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: DHS: We tricked schools into un-enrolling hundreds of thousands of visa students
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: DHS: We tricked schools into un-enrolling hundreds of thousands of visa students

notes: Needs context: the linked account describes hundreds of terminated SEVIS records, not hundreds of thousands, and does not establish that DHS admitted tricking schools. The exact case caption and a verified count are missing.
proposed_correction: Correct the headline to say a DHS filing stated that SEVIS termination did not itself end immigration status; remove “tricked” and “hundreds of thousands” unless supported by the filing and a reliable count.

title: After Chuck Schumer and Hakeem Jeffries met with Trump to discuss a
description_short: After Chuck Schumer and Hakeem Jeffries met with Trump to discuss a potential government shutdown, Trump posted an AI-generated video attacking Democratic politicians
description_medium: After a September 29, 2025, White House meeting about a looming shutdown, Donald Trump posted an apparently AI-generated video depicting Hakeem Jeffries in a sombrero and mustache and using a fake voice for Chuck Schumer. The video mocked Democratic leaders with false claims about healthcare and voting. Jeffries called the post bigoted; Schumer said it showed Trump could not negotiate. The meeting ended without a funding deal.
description_long: On September 29, 2025, President Donald Trump met at the White House with Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer and House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries, along with Republican congressional leaders, to discuss a looming government shutdown. The meeting ended without an agreement. Hours later, Trump posted an apparently AI-generated video on X and Truth Social that showed Jeffries in a sombrero and mustache and put words in a fake voice for Schumer. In the clip, the fabricated Schumer claimed Democrats wanted free healthcare for undocumented immigrants to win votes; it also repeated false Republican claims about Democratic policies. Jeffries responded that bigotry would not deter Democrats, while Schumer said the post showed Trump could only throw tantrums rather than negotiate. The video followed a real policy dispute over funding and Affordable Care Act subsidies. The incident joined that negotiation with a misleading, racially caricatured depiction of the opposition leaders. The post did not resolve the funding dispute, and the supplied report records no agreement after the meeting.

preserved_fields.description_short: After Chuck Schumer and Hakeem Jeffries met with Trump to discuss a potential government shutdown, Trump posted an AI-generated video attacking Democratic politicians
